---
title: "r-score"
description: "The r-score is the expected Pearson correlation between predicted and observed values of the test set, written in closed form for ridge regression."
---

The r-score is the expected Pearson correlation between predicted and observed values of the test set, written in closed form for ridge regression. It was introduced with this package.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Model-based |
| Direction | Larger is better |
| Uses a test set | yes |
| Score a given set | `r_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "rScore")` |

## Definition

With training matrix $X$ ($n \times p$, PCs or markers), test matrix $X_0$ with $n_0$ rows, and penalty $\lambda = 1/p$, the r-score is $q_{12}/\sqrt{q_1 q_2}$: the covariance of predicted and true test values over the product of their variances. Ou and Liao (2019) derive the three terms. TSDFGS evaluates them with a $p \times p$ matrix when $p \le n$ and an $n \times n$ matrix otherwise.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
r_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "rScore",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "rScore", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Ou, J.-H., & Liao, C.-T. (2019). Training set determination for genomic selection. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 132*, 2781-2792. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-019-03387-0>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** [github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS](https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS), the package of the method's authors.
